ease.reason: The n8n examples show invoice PDF extraction and sheet logging; a learner can test fictional files, while accuracy and setup are unverified.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small professional office may value less invoice handling; the vacancy establishes human work, not AI-service demand.

feasibility.reason: A two-week fictional PDF-to-review-table mock fits the attached extraction examples; accounting rules and live access are not established.

autonomy.reason: The examples document extraction and logging; staff must check fields and make all billing, payment and customer decisions.

evidence.reason: The notice names invoicing, customer follow-up and key-figure reporting; n8n examples show invoice extraction only, not business rules or AI buyers.

candidates.reason: Assessed a narrow fictional-invoice extraction and review-table experiment. The n8n sources support extraction and logging, but this resembles recent invoice experiments and the equal-weight mean is 5.2, below threshold; no post.

candidates.title: Prepare a record filing review list

ease.reason: The notice names registration, case logging and archiving, but no attached reference demonstrates those mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional office may value less filing effort; this notice does not establish demand for an AI service.

feasibility.reason: A fictional filing checklist is possible, but categories, document formats and rules are absent and no building reference applies.

autonomy.reason: A tool could format operator-entered rows, but a person must classify, verify and archive records; no repeatable automation is documented.

evidence.reason: The fresh notice states registration, case logging and archiving as chores, but gives no task detail or corroborating implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Concrete filing and registration duties are stated, but no relevant building reference supports a useful narrow workflow. The proposed synthetic checklist remains under threshold; an earlier filing-checklist attempt also found no adequate implementation support.
